_comment: Uses the same crypt.glb as the surface scene for now. Step 8 (asset split) will produce crypt_interior.glb (interior + descent only). With the same .glb, exterior and interior visually look the same — the architectural value of the scene split is logical (separate Jolt body sets, separate trigger volumes, separate ambient/sky/audio configs) until the .glb split lands.
_terrain_comment: Chapel interior loads the same terrain as the surface scene because terrain IS the chapel's interior floor (the plinth-top FlushAt modifier raises terrain to chapel-floor Y inside the chapel footprint, and the chapel mesh has no authored interior floor primitive). Without this, the player walks through the door and falls — chapel_interior would have no walkable surface inside the chapel. The descent shaft is carved through the terrain by the TerrainModifier::Hole at the upper-flight footprint, so the player can still fall through into the descent.
_terrain_modifiers_note: Chapel interior is not a terrain-bearing scene. No modifiers.

triggers._comment: Player walks back out through the chapel door, returns to surface scene. Position is at the chapel door's world XZ (chapel center 0, -210; front face at z = -210 + 4 = -206; trigger 1m IN FRONT of the door so it fires as player walks toward exit).

At the bottom of the continuous descent stairs, where the player steps onto the acheron platform. Position derived from descent geometry: top at world y=32, drops ~62m over chapel-local Y +143; world coords ~(0, -30, -353).
